title: Why North Korea is Probably Not Planning a War
summary: An arms-control expert discusses US nuclear modernisation, China's warhead buildup, North Korea's intentions and arms sales to Russia, and spreading proliferation.

assertions.quote: they're going from 300 to at least a thousand weapons
went out of his way to say we will not initiate a war

verdicts.note: Pyongyang has avoided full-scale war since 1953 and its doctrine stresses regime survival, though limited provocations continue.
Polymarket priced a North Korean offensive to take any part of South Korea before 2027 at 5.5%.

assertions.quote: he's reversed Decades of models of buying arms from Russia and now he's selling arms to Russia

verdicts.note: Ukrainian, South Korean and US intelligence and satellite imagery document millions of North Korean shells and many ballistic missiles sent to Russia.
EFIS: Russia has acquired an estimated 5-7 million artillery rounds from Iran and North Korea since 2023, with North Korean ammunition about half of Russian artillery fire in the second half of 2025.
US intelligence says North Korea's and Iran's military support to Russia has helped Moscow in its war against Ukraine (quantities not given).

assertions.quote: Putin went out of his way to signal that those kinds of uh that sort of assistance would be made available

verdicts.note: US and South Korean officials report Russian help, notably with satellites and air defence, but the extent of the transfers is not publicly verified.

The Bulletin expects Russian assistance to North Korea's nuclear and missile capabilities to expand, perhaps as a quid pro quo for North Korean soldiers rather than arms, and states it as likely rather than documented.
US intelligence says North Korean troops are gaining warfighting experience and military technology from Russia for taking part in the war.

assertions.quote: I believe deterrence by punishment Works
I am fundamentally a minimum deterrence person

verdicts.note: Minimum deterrence is a strategic judgment about what leaders fear; there is no test of how deterrence varies with arsenal size.

assertions.quote: we are about to run arm streat with the Russians and the Chinese
the technology to build nuclear weapons and missiles is so much easier to get

verdicts.note: Missile technology has clearly spread, as the Houthis show, but nuclear proliferation has stayed slow, with no new nuclear state since North Korea.

assertions.quote: I think we are all better off at a at a lower number of nuclear Powers

verdicts.note: Most scholars argue proliferation raises the odds of accident, theft and use, though a minority argue it spreads stability, and there is no clean test.

FRI participants said Iran getting nuclear weapons would raise their risk of nuclear catastrophe by about 50% (experts) or 20% (superforecasters), a non-state actor would double it, and any other new state would raise it 20-30%.

RAND argues the Cold War's essentially bipolar order encouraged crisis and arms-race stability, whereas today's nine nuclear states with overlapping rivalries aggravate instability; an expert judgement, not a measured effect.

assertions.quote: I am just really reluctant to spend $130 billion

verdicts.note: Whether the Sentinel missile is worth its rising cost is a budget and strategy judgment, not a testable fact.
